questions.q: Why does the summary say travel cannot solve your problems?
a: You take yourself with you, so inner troubles remain
New places bring unfamiliar problems of their own
Trips end too quickly to change anything
Tourists rarely meet local people
questions.why: Lesson 1 says travel makes a poor escape, since the problems you carry are internal.

questions.q: What happened to the fictional Jean des Esseintes?
a: He soaked up so much Britishness that he never boarded the train
He moved to London and abandoned his books
He wrote a guidebook about England
He returned home disappointed by the food
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes him visiting an English pub and feeling too worn out to make the trip.

Forgetting facts soon after learning them
Refusing to read anything before a trip
The stress of planning a tight itinerary
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes arriving armed with lists of sights, then zoning out from too much information.

questions.q: What does De Botton recommend instead of photographs and postcards?
a: Drawing scenes and writing long letters
Buying local artworks and souvenirs
Recording short videos to share later
Keeping a list of every place you visit
questions.why: Lesson 3 suggests drawing and long letters, following the practice of John Ruskin.

questions.q: Why does drawing help you appreciate a place?
a: It makes you process the scene longer, creating a vivid memory
It proves to others that you really visited
It is faster than taking a photo
It captures colors that cameras miss
questions.why: Lesson 3 says drawing gives you more time to process a scene with your senses and mind.
